correctness.rationale: For every broken directed cycle, scalar logistic induction constructs the sole Hurwitz equilibrium. At intact cycles, the unique positive equilibrium has eigenvalues -(1+sigma exp(2pi ik/n))/(1+sigma). At positive gain >1, transverse invasion inequalities force any Hurwitz boundary equilibrium to alternate zeros and ones, possible only on even cycles. These arguments produce every count; finite-edge-event probability and parity-geometric-series summation produce the full law and expectation. All 992 numerical support and spectral comparisons and the separate Bernoulli richness checks replay. Noncritical parameter boundaries stated.

value.rationale: Directly addresses a concrete model question in the source: distribution of the number of Hurwitz-stable ecological communities under independently random interactions. A single randomly deleted directed link restores a uniquely stable boundary community, whereas intact parity controls coexistence versus multiple stable extinction patterns. The exact all-size probability law and survivor expectation quantify the sharp rare-break scaling q=1-lambda/n, without presenting mere isolated numerical examples.
